You are shown THREE frames from a high-speed shadowgraphy video of a ~2 mm droplet impacting a superhydrophobic glass surface.

• Frame 1 — just BEFORE impact (droplet in free fall)
• Frame 2 — at MAXIMUM SPREADING (widest contact with surface)
• Frame 3 — AFTER REBOUND (droplet leaving or above the surface)

Study the visual dynamics carefully:
  – How far does the droplet spread?
  – Does it retract cleanly and bounce, or does it stick?
  – Does it fragment or leave a residue?
  – What is the droplet shape before and after impact?

Classify the fluid composition:

A) Pure water — deionised water, no additives
B) Surfactant solution only — water + surfactant (SDS / TX-100 / cocoglycoside), no nanoparticles
C) CA nanoparticles + surfactant — cellulose acetate nanoparticles synthesised WITH surfactant, surfactant still present in the droplet
D) Washed CA nanoparticles — CA nanoparticles prepared in surfactant then WASHED (no free surfactant remains in droplet)
